en: 5. The Question on the Ship “Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you said—that ‘three qualities should be taken from a ship’—which are those three qualities that should be taken?
“Just as, Great King, a ship carries many people across by means of the combination of various kinds of timber, so too...”

In the same way, Great King, the world together with its devas must be ferried across by the yogin, the practitioner of yoga, by means of the collection of various dharmas consisting of conduct, virtue, qualities, duties, and services.
This, Great King, is the first factor to be taken from the ship.
Furthermore, Great King, the ship endures the force of various kinds of waves, surging currents, whirlpools, and the force of tossing waters.
In the same way, Great King, the yogin, the practitioner of yoga, must endure the forceful waves of manifold defilements—

the gain, honor, fame, renown, worship, and salutation [received] from other families, as well as the censure and praise, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor, and the forceful waves of various faults. This, Great King,
is the second quality to be taken from the ship.

Furthermore, Great King, a ship travels upon the great ocean— which is immeasurable, infinite, shoreless, unshakeable, and deep, resounding with a vast roar, and teeming with shoals of timi, timingala, and makara fish— just so, Great King,
should the mind of a yogin, a practitioner of yoga, be directed toward the penetration and realization of the Four Noble Truths in their three turnings and twelve aspects.
This, Great King, is the third quality to be adopted from the ship.
“Great King, this was also spoken by the Blessed One, the God above gods, in the excellent Saṃyutta Nikāya, in the Saṃyutta on the Truths:
‘And when you reflect, monks, you should reflect: “This is suffering”; you should reflect: “This is the origin of suffering”; you should reflect:
“This is the cessation of suffering”; you should reflect: “This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering.”’”
The fifth question on the non-limbs.
